Table II illustrates the impact of community-engaged learning pedagogy on student retention. 
Notably, 85% of students indicated that their community-engaged learning class influenced their 
desire to graduate from UMass Dartmouth. This demonstrates that students perceive a strong 
connection between engaging in real-life projects and community challenges and the overall 
value of their educational experience at UMass Dartmouth. 
The University of Massachusetts Dartmouth has made great strides toward achieving its 
community-engaged learning strategic goals. We are recognized in our region and nationally 
as being at the forefront of engaged educational processes. There has been significant growth 
in faculty involvement and co-jointly a considerable increase in the number of class offerings 
using this pedagogy. We have grown community-engaged learning to a point where 82% of our 
graduating class in 2026 were exposed to this pedagogy. Community-engaged learning classes 
have helped the community address critical issues of educational attainment, environment, 
community development, youth development, health, economic development, and public safety.
